classification.difficultyReason: Use a six-period decrease factor and reverse it while distinguishing annual growth from total tree height.

content.prompt: The height of a mature tree is measured on the same day each year. Each year for the last six years, the growth has been 9% less than the previous year’s growth.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the percentage decrease in growth over the six years, correct to the nearest percent?

answer.worked:
Each year’s growth is 91% of the previous year’s growth.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage decrease}&=(1-0.91^6)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&=43.2130747959\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx43\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the growth this year was 320 mm, what was the growth six years ago, correct to the nearest millimetre?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Growth six years ago}&=320\div0.91^6\\\text{Growth six years ago}&\approx564\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$
